title: Double Consonants
subtitle: The phonemic length distinction: pala vs. palla, casa vs. cassa.
objectives: Distinguish single from double consonants by audible length.
Pronounce minimal pairs (pala/palla, pena/penna) without confusion.
Understand that doubling affects meaning, not just emphasis.

sections.heading: Length is meaning
sections.body: Italian double consonants are not mere emphasis. They are phonemic: they change the meaning of the word. pala (shovel) versus palla (ball); pena (penalty, pain) versus penna (pen); casa (house) versus cassa (box, till); fato (fate) versus fatto (done, fact). When you double a consonant in Italian, you hold it longer. A double t is not two separate t sounds; it is one t sound held for twice the duration. The same applies to double l, double n, double m, double r.

sections.heading: From Manzoni
sections.body: Alessandro Manzoni, I promessi sposi, chapter I: Quel ramo del lago di Como, che volge a mezzogiorno. volge: single l in the root (volgere), but if we had volle (he wanted, from volere), the double l would be audible. mezzogiorno: double z (held longer), double g in giorno. Boccaccio, Decameron, Proemio: Umana cosa è aver compassione degli afflitti. compassione: double s. afflitti: double f, double t. Each doubling is phonemic.

sections.heading: Listening drill
sections.instructions: Ten minimal pairs spoken in sequence. Repeat each one, holding the double consonant for audible length.

items.prompt: What is the difference between pala and palla?
items.answer: Single l (shovel) versus double l (ball). The double l is held longer.
ka.sa, kas.sa — hold the double s.
pe.na, pen.na — the double n is audible.
No. They are phonemic: they change meaning.

items.prompt: How do you produce a double consonant?
items.answer: Hold the consonant for twice the length of a single consonant. Do not release and restart; hold.

sections.heading: Words with doubles
sections.instructions: Read aloud; hold the doubled consonant.
